i|seat:sit|sit|peach:pitʃ|pitch|Raise the front of the tongue gently; move toward the vowel in sit and back.|siːt
ɪ|sit:sɪt|seat|pick:pɪk|peak|Relax the tongue slightly from the vowel in seat.|sɪt
ɛ|bed:bɛd|bad|pen:pɛn|pan|From an open jaw, raise it a little until the vowel sounds like bed.|bed
æ|bad:bæd|bed|pack:pæk|peck|Open the jaw farther than for bed; keep the tongue forward.|bæd
ʌ|cup:kʌp|cap|luck:lʌk|lock|Keep the stressed vowel central and your lips unrounded.|kʌp
ɑ|palm:pɑm|Pam|calm:kɑm|cam|Lower the jaw and move the tongue back; keep the vowel steady.|pɑːm
ɒ|pot:pɑt|put|sock:sɑk|suck|Compare the British rounded short vowel with the American vowel in pot.|pɒt
ɔ|caught:kɔt;kɑt|coat|taught:tɔt;tɑt|tote|Compare a steady vowel with the glide in coat. Both American cot–caught patterns are welcome.|kɔːt
ʊ|full:fʊl|fool|pull:pʊl|pool|Keep the lips lightly rounded and the tongue relaxed.|fʊl
u|food:fud|foot|pool:pul|pull|Round the lips and raise the tongue; compare with the vowel in foot.|fuːd
ɝ|bird:bɝd|board|turn:tɝn|torn|Let the vowel and the American r quality happen together.|bɜːd
ə|about:əˈbaʊt|a boat|above:əˈbʌv|a glove|Relax the first vowel and carry the main beat on the second syllable.|əˈbaʊt
eɪ|sale:seɪl|sell|late:leɪt|let|Start in an open mid position and glide toward a closer vowel.|seɪl
aɪ|time:taɪm|tame|ride:ɹaɪd|raid|Move from an open starting point to a higher front position.|taɪm
ɔɪ|coin:kɔɪn|cane|toy:tɔɪ|tie|Begin rounded and release the rounding as the tongue moves forward.|kɔɪn
aʊ|now:naʊ|no|loud:laʊd|load|Begin open, then move toward rounded lips in one syllable.|naʊ
oʊ|go:ɡoʊ|cow|coat:koʊt|cot|Round the lips toward the end of a single glide.|ɡəʊ
ɪɹ|near:nɪɹ|knee|dear:dɪɹ|day|In US speech, move from the vowel into r; compare the UK model without a final r.|nɪə
ɛɹ|care:kɛɹ|car|share:ʃɛɹ|shy|Keep the tongue in the vowel region for care before moving into American r.|keə
ʊɹ|tour:tʊɹ;tɔɹ|two|cure:kjʊɹ;kjɔɹ|cue|Listen for the r quality in American speech. The UK reference illustrates a different reading.|tʊə;tɔː
p|pack:pæk|back|pin:pɪn|bin|Close both lips, then release them together.|pæk
b|back:bæk|pack|bin:bɪn|pin|Make a brief closure with both lips; compare the release with pack.|bæk
t|ten:tɛn|den|tie:taɪ|die|Touch the ridge behind the teeth and release cleanly.|ten
d|den:dɛn|ten|day:deɪ|they|Make a short tongue-tip closure at the ridge and allow voice to continue.|den
k|key:ki|tea|coat:koʊt|goat|Use the back of the tongue for the closure; keep the tip free.|kiː
ɡ|gate:ɡeɪt|Kate|goat:ɡoʊt|coat|Keep the back closure from key and compare the voicing and release.|ɡeɪt
s|sip:sɪp|ship|ice:aɪs|eyes|Direct a narrow stream of air forward near the tooth ridge.|sɪp
z|rise:ɹaɪz|rice|buzz:bʌz|bus|Keep the friction while adding voice; listen to the preceding vowel too.|raɪz
ʃ|ship:ʃɪp|sip|cash:kæʃ|catch|Raise a broader part of the tongue and let air flow continuously.|ʃɪp
ʒ|vision:ˈvɪʒən|mission|measure:ˈmɛʒɚ|major|Start with the friction in sh, then add voicing without making a closure.|ˈvɪʒən
tʃ|chin:tʃɪn|shin|catch:kætʃ|cash|Begin with a closure and release into friction in a single movement.|tʃɪn
dʒ|joke:dʒoʊk|choke|jeep:dʒip|cheap|Release a voiced closure into friction. Compare its beginning with sh.|dʒəʊk
f|fan:fæn|van|fine:faɪn|vine|Touch upper teeth lightly to the lower lip and let air pass.|fæn
v|van:væn|fan|vine:vaɪn|fine|Use the same light lip contact as f and add voicing.|væn
w|wet:wɛt|vet|west:wɛst|vest|Round the lips then move straight into the next vowel.|wet
j|yes:jɛs|guess|yet:jɛt|get|Begin with the tongue high and front and glide quickly into the vowel.|jes
h|hat:hæt|at|heat:hit|eat|Shape the coming vowel while letting breath escape first.|hæt
θ|thin:θɪn|tin|thick:θɪk|tick|Rest the tongue lightly at the teeth and let air continue past it.|θɪn
ð|they:ðeɪ|day|then:ðɛn|den|Let the tongue approach the teeth lightly and add voice to the airflow.|ðeɪ
m|map:mæp|nap|meal:mil|kneel|Close the lips and let the voice resonate through the nose.|mæp
n|net:nɛt|met|night:naɪt|might|Keep the lips open and make the closure at the tooth ridge.|net
ŋ|sing:sɪŋ|sin|rang:ɹæŋ|ran|Close the back of the tongue and keep the nasal sound through the ending.|sɪŋ
l|light:laɪt|right|lane:leɪn|rain|Let air pass at the sides while the tongue tip touches the ridge.|laɪt
ɹ|red:ɹɛd|led|road:ɹoʊd|load|Bring the tongue into your comfortable r position and leave space for air.|red
ɚ|teacher:ˈtitʃɚ|teaching|letter:ˈlɛtɚ|letting|Keep the ending relaxed and r-colored in American speech.|ˈtiːtʃə
